agent: guicontainers - CFixedWindow +0x414 against +0x2FC, and every CWindowType::LoadKey token tied to its container, 2026-10-02
question: FINDINGS-guistatic.md's open items 4 and 5: read 0xAC4580/0xAC4640 and whatever fills CFixedWindow +0x414, decide whether +0x414 and not +0x2FC is the real child-window container, and tie each of CWindowType::LoadKey's child keywords to its container so the three `likely` keyword attributions become readable facts.

addresses.name: SubWindowMap_Contains
addresses.comment:
Whether a CFixedWindow's subwindow map holds an entry under this name. The map is the three-pointer vector at complete CFixedWindow +0x414 ({begin, end, capacity_end}) whose elements are 0x20 bytes, {Hoi3CString name at +0; CFixedWindow* window at +0x1C} - so this is a linear scan from [map] to [map+4] at a 0x20 stride, comparing the key against each element's own string. The compare is 0x415F70 (memcmp with the pointers in ECX and EDX and the length pushed), guarded by the usual MSVC std::string length test, and the SSO branch (`if capacity >= 0x10 then the buffer is at +0 else the object is the buffer`) appears on both sides.

Two stack arguments and `ret 8` on both exits, nothing in ecx, so __stdcall. Returns `al`: 1 on a match at 0xAC45F7, 0 at 0xAC4604 when the walk runs off the end.

It is a template body and takes its container as an argument, so the name is from its only use, not from the body: **all four of its call sites pass CFixedWindow +0x414** (0xAC1004 in the constructor's resolve loop, 0xAC2BCD in CFixedWindow::FindChild, 0xAC2C51 in CFixedWindow::GetSubWindow, 0xAC3FC7 in the CGuiObject slot 37 descendant test), and 'subwindow' is the engine's own word for what that container holds - 0xAC2C20 logs 'Warning: Atempt to access nonexistant subwindow ' from fixedwindow.cpp line 1042 when this returns 0. Every site pairs it immediately with SubWindowMap_FindOrAdd (0x6C4640), which inserts on a miss, which is why the guard exists at all.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled whole, 0xAC4580..0xAC460A, both exits `ret 8`. findRefs.py --callers gives exactly four callers and all four compute the container as `lea reg, [window + 0x414]` or `add reg, 0x3FC` on the CGuiObject-relative pointer (0x3FC + 0x18 = 0x414). The 0x20 stride is the `add edi, 0x20` at 0xAC45F2; the element's string at +0 is the `[edi+0x10]`/`[edi+0x14]` size/capacity pair at 0xAC45B7/0xAC45C9, which is MSVC's std::string layout and the same pair the key is read with at 0xAC45A4/0xAC45AC. Would be shown wrong by: a fifth call site passing some other container, or an element whose +0 is not a string (the +0x10/+0x14 reads would then be garbage and the compare length nonsense).

addresses.name: SubWindowMap_FindOrAdd
addresses.comment:
The subwindow map's `operator[]`: the same linear scan as SubWindowMap_Contains over CFixedWindow +0x414, but it returns a **pointer to the entry's value slot** - `lea eax, [edi + 0x1C]` at 0xAC46D0 - and on a miss it **appends a default entry under that name and returns the new slot** rather than failing. The miss path builds an empty Hoi3CString (0x401BD0), hands the 0x20-byte pair to the vector insert 0x542FC0 (which takes the vector in EDI, so `mov edi, esi` at 0xAC4716 first), and then computes the result as `begin + ((end - begin) & ~0x1F) - 4`, i.e. the last element's +0x1C.

Because it inserts, it is never safe on its own, and four of its five callers guard it with SubWindowMap_Contains first and dereference `[eax]` only when that said yes. The fifth, 0x7FC3FC, calls it unguarded on `[this+0xA8] + 0x414` with a name made by converting an integer to a decimal string (0xB9A0C4, radix 10) - numbered subwindows - and then dereferences `[eax]` and calls slot 20 on it, so that site relies on the entry existing.

Two stack arguments, `ret 8` on both exits, nothing in ecx, so __stdcall, with its own SEH frame (handler 0xC14BD8) around the temporary string. The name is from the container, as for 0x6C4580: all five call sites pass CFixedWindow +0x414.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled whole, 0xAC4640..0xAC4750, both exits `ret 8`. The match path returns `edi + 0x1C` where edi walks at a 0x20 stride from [map] to [map+4] - that is the value slot of a {string(0x1C), pointer(4)} pair. The miss path's `and ecx, 0xFFFFFFE0` on `end - begin` is the compiler's divide-by-0x20, which is independent corroboration of the 0x20 element size. findRefs.py --callers gives five callers; four are 0xAC100F, 0xAC2BD8, 0xAC2C5C, 0xAC3FD2, each five bytes after a SubWindowMap_Contains call on the same `lea` of +0x414, and the fifth is 0x7FC3FC on `[this+0xA8] + 0x414`. Would be shown wrong by: a caller that treats the return as the entry rather than the value (it would then read the name as a pointer), or by 0x542FC0 turning out not to append (the returned `end - 4` would then not be the new entry).

addresses.name: SubWindowMap_Add
addresses.signature: void __stdcall SubWindowMap_Add(Hoi3CString* name, CFixedWindow** window, void* map@EDI)
addresses.comment:
Appends one {name, window} entry to a CFixedWindow's subwindow map. Builds the 0x20-byte pair on its own stack - an Hoi3CString assigned from `name` (0x401BD0) at +0, then the dword at `*window` written into +0x1C - and hands it to the vector insert 0x542FC0, which takes the vector in **EDI**, so the container reaches this function in EDI too and never touches the stack. `ret 8`, two stack arguments, own SEH frame.

Its only caller is the CFixedWindow constructor's subwindow build loop at 0xAC0C86, with `lea edi, [this + 0x414]` set up three instructions earlier - which is what makes the register argument readable at all.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled whole, 0xAC44F0..0xAC456E, single exit `ret 8`. [ebp+8] goes to 0x401BD0 (recorded as std::string::assignString) as the source string; [ebp+0xC] is dereferenced once and the dword stored at pair+0x1C. findRefs.py --callers gives exactly one caller, 0xAC0C86, inside CFixedWindow::CFixedWindow, where edi was loaded with `lea edi, [ebx + 0x414]` at 0xAC0C7D and ebx is the `this` the constructor took from [ebp+8]. The EDI convention matches the already-recorded std::vector_pushBackByAddress (0x46CC20, `vector@EDI`), which is the pointer-element version of the same template. Would be shown wrong by: a second caller that puts something else in EDI, or by the pair's +0x1C turning out to be part of the string rather than the value - the stack arithmetic (`sub esp, 0x24`, string at base+0, `mov [esp+0x1C], edx` once esp is back at base) is what rules that out.

addresses.name: CFixedWindow::GetSubWindow
addresses.comment:
Looks one **subwindow** up by name and returns it, or 0 after logging. CFixedWindow primary vftable slot 27. The only container it touches is the map at complete +0x414: SubWindowMap_Contains, then SubWindowMap_FindOrAdd, then `mov eax, [eax]` and return - so the value really is the complete CFixedWindow pointer, with no CGuiObject adjustment (unlike slot 12, which adds 0x18).

**This function is where the engine names the container.** On a miss it builds 'fixedwindow.cpp' (0x1601DB0) with line 0x412 = 1042, logs 'Warning: Atempt to access nonexistant subwindow ' (0x1601DF4, the engine's own spelling, misspelling included) followed by the name and ' in window 2 ' (0x1601DE4) and the window's own name from `[this+0x3C]->vf[6]`, raises it through 0xA64A30 at severity 0x30, and returns 0 at 0xAC2D6A. That log line is the evidence for calling +0x414 the subwindow map rather than naming it after what it happens to hold.

`ret 4`, receiver in ecx as the **complete** object (every displacement in the body is a complete-object offset).
addresses.evidence: Disassembled whole, 0xAC2C20..0xAC2D77. Reading 0x1601F88 + 27*4 out of the image gives 0xAC2C20, and vtable.py --holding puts the body in exactly one RTTI table, CEU3DialogGui slot 27 (object offset 0) - the GUI framework has no RTTI of its own, which is why the export knows the table only through that derived class. findRefs.py --callers gives zero direct callers, consistent with a slot reached only virtually. The two string pushes at 0xAC2C7E and 0xAC2CC1 are the file name and the warning, and 0xAC2C7E is one of the two sites FINDINGS-guistatic.md already used as its positive control that fixedwindow.cpp brackets CFixedWindow's code. Would be shown wrong by: the log text belonging to a different container in the same body - it does not, +0x414 is the only container this function reads.

addresses.name: CFixedWindow::FindChild
addresses.comment:
Finds any child of the window by name, over every container it has, and returns it as a CGuiObject* - the general lookup of which GetSubWindow (slot 27) is the subwindow-only special case. CFixedWindow primary vftable slot 12. Searches in this fixed order and stops at the first hit:

    1  vector pair +0x25C / +0x26C   (guiButtonType children)        0xAC47C0
    2  vector pair +0x27C / +0x28C   (multiSpriteButtonType)         0xAC47C0
    3  registry +0x360               (3dButtonType)                  slot 1
    4  registry +0x33C               (textBoxType)                   slot 1
    5  registry +0x384               (editBoxType)                   slot 1
    6  map +0x414                    (subwindows)        result [eax] + 0x18
    7  vector pair +0x2FC / +0x30C   (attached through slot 22)      0xAC47C0

The `+ 0x18` on step 6 and nowhere else is the whole point: a subwindow is stored as a **complete** CFixedWindow pointer and has to be converted to its CGuiObject subobject, while every other container already holds CGuiObject pointers. A null value in the map is returned as 0 rather than as 0x18.

`ret 4`, receiver in ecx as the complete object. Three early `ret 4`s inside the body (0xAC2B67, 0xAC2B95, 0xAC2BC3) are the registry hits, not abutting functions - trap 2 checked.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled whole, 0xAC2AF0..0xAC2C12; image.retsBefore(0xAC2AF0, 0xAC2BCD) returns three `ret 4`s and each is preceded by the same `pop ebx/edi/esi/ebp` epilogue inside one frame, so they are this function's exits and not a boundary. Reading 0x1601F88 + 12*4 gives 0xAC2AF0; vtable.py --holding puts it in CEU3DialogGui slot 12 (object offset 0) and nowhere else. The seven container offsets are read straight off the `lea`s at 0xAC2AFA, 0xAC2B1A, 0xAC2B3A, 0xAC2B6A, 0xAC2B98, 0xAC2BC6 and 0xAC2BF6. Would be shown wrong by: the +0x18 at 0xAC2BE5 applying to something other than the map's value, or by a container this misses - the body has no other memory operand above +0x200.

addresses.name: CWindowType::CreateWindow
addresses.signature: CFixedWindow* __thiscall CWindowType::CreateWindow(Hoi3CString name, void* param2, void* param3)
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0xAC76D0..0xAC77E2, single exit `ret 0x24`. 0xAC4FE0, the function it calls at 0xAC77A2, begins `push 0x4C8; call 0xB9602F` and ends by calling 0xABF8E0, which project.json already records as CFixedWindow::CFixedWindow - so the object built is a CFixedWindow and its size is 0x4C8. `lea ebx, [esi + 0x18]` at 0xAC77AD is the complete-to-CGuiObject adjustment CFixedWindow's own constructor uses (`lea eax, [ebx + 0x18]; call 0xA7FF60` at 0xABF923). CWindowType +0x150 holds vftable 0x1602108, written by the CWindowType constructor at 0xAC49C8 - the same embedded name tree as CGui +0x34. The 0x24 arithmetic: 0x1C for the by-value string plus 8 for the two dwords. findRefs.py --callers gives exactly two. Would be shown wrong by: 0xAC4FE0 allocating something other than a CFixedWindow, or the [ebp+8] block not being one string (the caller at 0xAC0C4A does `sub esp, 0x1C` and constructs a string there, which is what settles it).

addresses.name: CWindowType::CWindowType
addresses.signature: CWindowType* __stdcall CWindowType::CWindowType(CWindowType* this, void* inherited@ECX, CGui* gui@EDX)
addresses.comment:
The CWindowType constructor. Writes vftable 0x1602178 at +0 and 0x16021A4 at +0x64, sets the type id at +4 to 0x18D, stores its two register arguments at +0x148 and +0x14C, plants the embedded gui-type name tree at +0x150 (vftable 0x1602108, root +0x154, mode byte +0x158), and then zeroes the whole child-type area: the pointer vector at +0x174, the thirteen per-kind declared-name lists at +0x184 through +0x244 ({head, tail, count, byte} at a 0x10 stride), the two bytes at +0x254/+0x255, the orientation pointer at +0x258, the shared declaration-order list at +0x25C and the two sound strings at +0x26C and +0x288.

**CWindowType is 0x2A4 bytes** and the class is recursive: LoadKey's `windowType` case allocates 0x2A4 and calls this, so a window type's child window types are CWindowTypes in turn.

`this` arrives on the **stack** at [ebp+8], not in ecx, and the function returns it in eax - hence __stdcall with an explicit `this` parameter rather than __thiscall. ecx and edx are untouched between entry and the stores at 0xAC49BC/0xAC49C2, so both really are incoming register arguments; edx is the CGui (CWindowType::CreateWindow calls slots 16 and 18 on +0x14C), and what +0x148 is has not been settled. Three callers: 0xAC623A (LoadKey's `windowType` case), 0x6436D6 and 0xA7D8E1.
addresses.evidence: 0x1602178 slot 4 is 0xAC55E0, which project.json already records as CWindowType::LoadKey - so 0x1602178 is CWindowType's own table and 0xAC48C0, which writes it, is CWindowType's constructor. checkSignatures.py's constructor rule is satisfied by construction. Exit `ret 4` at 0xAC4C2E with `mov eax, esi` (esi = [ebp+8]) at 0xAC4C20; 0xAC4C40 is the scalar-deleting destructor that follows it, and it is slot 0 of the same table, so the `ret 4` really is the end (trap 3 checked that way). The 0x2A4 size is the `push 0x2A4; call 0xB9602F` at 0xAC6212 immediately before the only call site that can be read in context. A scan of 0xAC48C0..0xAC49C8 for any write to ecx or edx returns nothing. Would be shown wrong by: an instruction between entry and 0xAC49BC loading ecx or edx (there is none), or by 0x1602178 slot 4 belonging to a base class that also happens to hold LoadKey.

struct_fields.name: subwindows_begin
struct_fields.comment:
**Begin of the window's subwindow map - the container that really holds the child windows the .gui file declares, and not +0x2FC.** A std::vector of 0x20-byte entries, {Hoi3CString name at +0; CFixedWindow* window at +0x1C}, used as a name-keyed map: SubWindowMap_Contains (0x6C4580) tests a key, SubWindowMap_FindOrAdd (0x6C4640) returns the value slot, SubWindowMap_Add (0x6C44F0) appends. Complete-object offset; the pointer CGui +0x5C hands you is complete+0x18, so this is +0x3FC from it.

Filled only by the CFixedWindow constructor's build loop at 0xAC0C33..0xAC0C90, which walks the name list the constructor was handed in its 11th argument - that argument is `&CWindowType +0x214`, the `windowType` keyword's declared-name list - and for each name calls CWindowType::CreateWindow (0x6C76D0) on the window's own type at +0x88 and adds the result here under that name.

The value is a **complete** CFixedWindow pointer: CFixedWindow::FindChild adds 0x18 to it to get a CGuiObject, the show and hide walks read `[entry+0x1C]` and then call CGuiObject slot 13 with `this = value + 0x18`, and CGuiObject slot 37's recursion does the same. 'Subwindow' is the engine's own word, from the warning CFixedWindow::GetSubWindow logs at fixedwindow.cpp line 1042.

+0x418 is the end and +0x41C the capacity end.
struct_fields.evidence: All three pointers zeroed together by the constructor at 0xABFCD0/0xABFCD6/0xABFCDC. The 0x20 stride and the {string, value} element are read three independent ways: the `add edi, 0x20` walks in 0x6C4580, 0x6C4640, 0xAC27C8 (show) and 0xAC3FF0 (slot 37); the `lea eax, [edi + 0x1C]` return in 0x6C4640; and the `and ecx, 0xFFFFFFE0` divide in both 0x6C4640 and the insert 0x542FC0. The windowType link was checked by counting the window factory 0xAC4FE0's pushes: 26 of them, matching the constructor's `ret 0x68`, and the one that lands at [ebp+0x44] - the slot the build loop reads - is `lea ecx, [esi + 0x214]` at 0xAC506E, where esi is the CWindowType. Would be shown wrong by: a 27th push or an `esp` adjustment between 0xAC501A and 0xAC50D2 (there is none), or a second writer of +0x414 - the only ones in the image are the constructor's loop, the destructor's teardown at 0xAC13D2..0xAC140A and SubWindowMap_Add.

struct_fields.name: subwindows_end
struct_fields.comment: End of the subwindow map at +0x414. Every walk of the map compares its cursor against this. (end - begin) / 0x20 is the subwindow count.
struct_fields.evidence: Zeroed with begin and capacity end at 0xABFCD6. Read as the loop bound at 0xAC459C, 0xAC4676, 0xAC27D0 and 0xAC3FF4, always against a cursor stepping 0x20. Would be shown wrong by a walk that used it as anything but a bound.

struct_fields.name: subwindows_capacity_end
struct_fields.comment:
Capacity end of the subwindow map at +0x414 - the third pointer of the vector. Read only by the insert helper 0x542FC0, which compares the end against it to decide whether to grow.

**Do not confuse it with the CGuiObject-relative +0x41C**, which is complete +0x434, `three_d_button_names`. CFixedWindow::Show and CFixedWindow::Hide both read `[esi+0x41C]` with esi as the CGuiObject subobject and that is the name list, not this field.
struct_fields.evidence: Zeroed with the other two at 0xABFCDC and cleared again by the destructor at 0xAC140A. `cmp eax, [edi+8]` at 0x542FEE with edi = the container is the grow test. The CGuiObject-relative warning is from reading Show at 0xAC27EB, where `[esi+0x41C]` is followed by `[esi+0x348]` - complete +0x360, the 3dButtonType registry - which is the name-list/registry pairing, 0x18 below throughout.

struct_fields.name: parent
struct_fields.comment: `parent = "..."` from the .gui file - the name of the type this one inherits from. Written by CWindowType::LoadKey's token 132 case at 0xAC5721 through ParseString. CWindowType::CreateWindow passes it to the CGui's slot 18 when a child window's own type is not in the tree at +0x150, so it is the fallback type as well as a declared field.
struct_fields.evidence: 0xAC5726 `add ebx, 0x68; push ebx; call 0xA7AFB0` in the case the jump table at 0xAC6A5C reaches for token 132, which ghidra/saveTokens.json spells `parent`. 0xA7AFB0 is already recorded as ParseString. The offset chain corroborates: +0x68 + 0x1C (Hoi3CString's size) = +0x84, the next string field, and so on up to +0x124. Would be shown wrong by the byte table at 0xAC6AB8 sending token 132 somewhere else.

struct_fields.name: background

Fits the string chain exactly: +0xA8 size is int[2] (already recorded), +0xB0 then +0xCC then +0xE8 then +0x104 at Hoi3CString's 0x1C stride, and +0x104 + 0x1C = +0x120, leaving +0x124 for the next scalar.

struct_fields.name: priority
struct_fields.comment: `priority = N` from the .gui file - the window's draw and hit-test order. Written by CWindowType::LoadKey's token 138 case at 0xAC5676, through 0x67B640, which is a parse helper not yet recorded (it is not ParseInt; it goes through 0xB964D4 with the format string at 0x15FD134).
struct_fields.evidence: 0xAC5679 `lea eax, [ebx + 0x124]; call 0xA7B640` for token 138 (`priority`). struct_fields.name: moveable
struct_fields.comment: `moveable = N` from the .gui file - whether the player can drag the window. struct_fields.evidence: 0xAC569A `lea eax, [ebx + 0x128]; call 0xA7B470` for token 154 (`moveable`); 0xA7B470 is recorded as `void __cdecl ParseInt(CParseContext* parse@ECX, int* out@EAX)`, which fixes both the width and the type. Would be shown wrong by a second writer of +0x128 of a different width.

struct_fields.name: gui_button_names
struct_fields.comment:
Head of the declared-name list for this window type's `guiButtonType` children - the first of **thirteen** per-kind lists at a 0x10 stride from +0x184 to +0x244, each {head, tail, count, byte} with the tail at +4 and the count at +8.

The nodes are 0x28 bytes: the child's name as an Hoi3CString at +0, prev at +0x1C, next at +0x20, a byte at +0x24. **The list holds names, not objects** - each child type built by LoadKey is inserted into the one gui-type tree at CWindowType +0x150 and only its name is listed here, which is why CFixedWindow::CreateWindow and the six per-kind factories all look a name up in that tree.

The CFixedWindow constructor copies this list, node by node through 0x409D00, into the window's own +0x25C/+0x26C vector pair: so **CFixedWindow +0x25C holds exactly the window's `guiButtonType` children**, which settles what project.json's `child_buttons_begin` is a vector of.

*FINDINGS-guistatic.md said fourteen containers running from +0x174; that is wrong twice. There are thirteen and they start at +0x184. +0x174 is a separate three-pointer std::vector walked at a 4-byte stride, and the fourteenth participant is the all-kinds declaration-order list at +0x25C.*
struct_fields.evidence: LoadKey's token 124 case (`guiButtonType` in ghidra/saveTokens.json, reached through the byte table at 0xAC6AB8 and the jump table at 0xAC6A5C) builds its child type with 0xB2DA90 and appends to this list at 0xAC5A48/0xAC5A4E/0xAC5A60. The node shape is from the `windowType` case, which is the same code with different offsets: `push 0x28; call operator_new` at 0xAC629A, string at node+0, prev from the old tail at node+0x1C, `[node+0x20] = 0` and `[node+0x24] = 0`, then the old tail's +0x20 set to the new node at 0xAC6312. The constructor copy is at 0xABFCE2 for the +0x424 pair and at 0xAC0822 for the +0x25C pair, both reading the argument the factory loaded with `lea edx, [esi + 0x184]` at 0xAC50AE - which lands at [ebp+0x20], the slot 0xAC0822 reads. The thirteen-not-fourteen correction: a scan of 0xABE000..0xAC9000 from int3-delimited entries for displacements 0x174/0x178/0x17C finds only the CWindowType constructor, destructor and slot 7, and slot 7 walks it with `add esi, 4` and `mov ecx, [esi]`, which is a pointer vector and not a 0x10 container.

struct_fields.name: multi_sprite_button_names
struct_fields.comment:
Head of the declared-name list for this window type's `multiSpriteButtonType` children. Second of the thirteen; same {head, tail, count, byte} shape as +0x184.

**This settles FINDINGS-guistatic.md's third `likely`.** The CFixedWindow constructor copies this list into the vector pair at window +0x27C / +0x28C, which project.json currently calls `child_vector_unused` - so that vector is the `multiSpriteButtonType` children's, and it is empty on every live window because the keyword occurs in no .gui file the game or the mod ships, not because its purpose was unknown.

struct_fields.name: child_window_names
struct_fields.comment:
Head of the declared-name list for this window type's **`windowType`** children - the tenth of the thirteen, and the one that answers FINDINGS-guistatic.md's open item 5.

Its children are themselves CWindowTypes: LoadKey's `windowType` case does `operator new(0x2A4)` and calls CWindowType::CWindowType, so the type tree is recursive. The CFixedWindow constructor is handed `&this+0x214` as its 11th stack argument and walks it at 0xAC0C33..0xAC0C90, building a full CFixedWindow per name through CWindowType::CreateWindow and adding each one to the window's **subwindow map at +0x414**.

So the chain `windowType` keyword -> CWindowType +0x214 -> CFixedWindow +0x414 is complete, and **CFixedWindow +0x2FC is not on it**. +0x2FC is written only by CFixedWindow::AttachChild (slot 22) and erased only by slot 23, so it holds what game code attaches at run time, which is why a live snapshot found buttons and icons in it.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadKey's token 152 case (`windowType` in ghidra/saveTokens.json) appends here at 0xAC62FF/0xAC6305/0xAC6317 after `push 0x2A4; call 0xB9602F; call 0xAC48C0` at 0xAC6212..0xAC623A. The window link is the push count: the factory 0xAC4FE0 makes exactly 26 pushes between 0xAC501A and 0xAC50D2 with no intervening call or esp adjustment, matching the constructor's `ret 0x68`, and the push that lands at [ebp+0x44] is `lea ecx, [esi + 0x214]` at 0xAC506E; [ebp+0x44] is what 0xAC0C33 reads. The constructor's loop then calls 0xAC76D0 (which allocates 0x4C8 and runs CFixedWindow::CFixedWindow) and 0xAC44F0 with `lea edi, [ebx + 0x414]`. Would be shown wrong by a 27th push, by an esp adjustment in that range, or by a second writer of CFixedWindow +0x414 - a scan of 0xABE000..0xAC9000 finds only the constructor's loop, the destructor and SubWindowMap_Add.

Written by CWindowType::LoadKey's token 321 case at 0xAC6A17 through ParseString. Exactly 0x1C above up_sound, so the two strings are adjacent and +0x288 + 0x1C = +0x2A4, which is the whole size of the class.

The CWindowType constructor initialises a string at +0x288 (`lea ecx, [esi + 0x288]` at 0xAC4B84), and it is the last member it touches. 0x288 + 0x1C = 0x2A4 = the `operator new` size at 0xAC6212, so this really is the end of the object.

slots_noted: 0xAC2C20 and 0xAC2AF0 are recorded under CEU3DialogGui because CFixedWindow has no RTTI table of its own - the GUI framework was compiled without RTTI - so the export knows CFixedWindow's tables only through the one derived class that does carry RTTI. The bodies are CFixedWindow's: reading 0x1601F88 + 27*4 and 0x1601F88 + 12*4 out of the image gives the same two addresses, and both bodies read CFixedWindow's own containers (+0x414, +0x2FC, +0x360) at complete-object offsets. This is the same arrangement FINDINGS-guistatic.md used for slots 22 and 36. The other five functions in this fragment (0x6C4580, 0x6C4640, 0x6C44F0, 0x6C76D0, 0x6C48C0) are in no virtual table at all, checked with vtable.py --holding.
